summary: After the exact sum/difference transform U=X-X', V=X+X' for cap-one finite-fragment extreme inputs, the conditional cap is M(u)=1/[2|E intersect (E-u)|]. For E_N=union_{k=1}^N[4^k,4^k+1/N], the exact moment is E[M(U)^alpha]=2^(1-alpha)/(2-alpha)[(1-1/N)N^alpha+1/N] for 0<alpha<2, while it is infinite for alpha>=2. Hence any proof that normalizes conjugate-variable fibers and then pays any positive power of their conditional density cap is non-uniform under the target hypotheses. This does not refute QFORM; it requires aggregate-before-normalization/coupled-pair methods.
